testName: Class B Knowledge Test #1 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: The air compressor governor controls:

options.text: When the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.
How fast air is pumped into the storage tanks.
The temperature of the air going into the storage tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor controls when air is pumped into the storage tanks in an air brake system.

questions.question: When you start an engine, oil pressure should reach a normal level:
questions.correctAnswerText: Within seconds.
questions.explanation: Check your gauges when you start the engine. Oil pressure should reach a normal level within seconds.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, you must check all of the following except:

options.text: That the oil pressure gauge works.
That the oil pressure warning light turns off or the gauge shows normal pressure.
That the oil temperature gauge rises to normal operating range.
That the oil pressure gauge comes on when brakes are used.

questions.correctAnswerText: That the oil pressure gauge comes on when brakes are used.
questions.explanation: During a vehicle inspection, check that the oil pressure gauge works. The gauge should show normal pressure or the warning light should turn off. If equipped, the oil temperature gauge should rise to normal operating range.

questions.question: If a vehicle begins to hydroplane, the driver should:

options.text: Release the accelerator and push in the clutch.
Push in the clutch and brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the accelerator and push in the clutch.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle hydroplanes, release the accelerator and push in the clutch to regain control.

questions.question: A vehicle inspection:

options.text: Helps catch small problems before they become big ones.
Should not be done by the driver.
Should be done once a month.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps catch small problems before they become big ones.
questions.explanation: Inspect your vehicle before every trip. This helps you find small problems before they become serious issues.

questions.question: Heavy vibration may mean a tire has failed.
questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: If your vehicle thumps or vibrates a lot, a tire may have failed. Check your tires as soon as you can safely pull over.

questions.question: Driving too fast:

options.text: Is a major cause of fatal crashes.
Can get you to your destination quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is a major cause of fatal crashes.
questions.explanation: Speeding is a major cause of deadly crashes. Never drive faster than the speed limit and adjust your speed for conditions.

questions.question: Bracing is used to:

options.text: Make items taller in a trailer.
Stop items from moving in a trailer.
Make it easier to unload items from a trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop items from moving in a trailer.
questions.explanation: Bracing stops cargo from shifting during transport. Bracing extends from the top of cargo to the floor and sides of the cargo space.

questions.question: A skid caused by acceleration can usually be fixed by:

options.text: Taking your foot off the accelerator.

questions.correctAnswerText: Taking your foot off the accelerator.
questions.explanation: Take your foot off the accelerator to correct a skid caused by acceleration. On very slippery surfaces, you may also need to push in the clutch.

questions.question: If your personal driver's license is revoked or suspended:

options.text: You can get a hardship license to drive a CMV.
You cannot get a hardship license to drive a CMV.
Your CDL will not be affected.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot get a hardship license to drive a CMV.
questions.explanation: If your personal driver's license is revoked, canceled, or suspended, you cannot get a hardship license to drive a CMV.

questions.question: If you hear or feel an unusual noise while driving, you should:

options.text: Hope the vehicle lasts until another driver takes over.
Stop and check what is wrong.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and check what is wrong.
questions.explanation: Pay attention to what you see, hear, smell, and feel while driving. If something seems wrong, stop and check it out right away.

questions.question: What can affect how far a vehicle travels before it stops?

options.text: What time of day it is.

questions.correctAnswerText: How fast you are driving.
questions.explanation: How far your vehicle travels before stopping depends on your speed, the vehicle's weight, and how much grip the road has.

questions.question: What should you do after finishing a trip?

options.text: Put the vehicle out of service.

questions.correctAnswerText: Complete an after-trip inspection.
questions.explanation: After each trip, you must inspect the vehicle and file a report about its condition.

questions.question: Exercise helps a person sober up after drinking alcohol.
questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Your liver removes alcohol at a fixed rate. Exercise, cold showers, and other tricks do not speed this up. Only time will make you sober.

questions.question: A safety belt:

options.text: Keeps you secure during a crash.
Allows you to be thrown inside your vehicle during a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keeps you secure during a crash.
questions.explanation: In a crash, a safety belt keeps you in your seat behind the steering wheel. This protects you from injury and helps you stay in control of the vehicle.

questions.question: Both systems in a dual air brake system share:
questions.correctAnswerText: An air compressor.
questions.explanation: Both systems share one air compressor. If the compressor breaks, neither system will work.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver crashes ahead of you, you should:

options.text: Pull over and yell at them.
Stop safely away from the crash and tell police about the aggressive driving.
Block the driver in with your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop safely away from the crash and tell police about the aggressive driving.
questions.explanation: If you see a crash involving aggressive driving, stay at a safe distance, wait for police, and tell them what you saw.

questions.question: An air compressor governor controls:

options.text: When air is pumped into the air storage tanks.
How fast air is pumped into the air storage tanks.
The temperature of the air pumped into the storage tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: When air is pumped into the air storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor decides when to pump air into the storage tanks.

questions.question: Brake fade happens because of:
questions.correctAnswerText: Using the brakes too much.
questions.explanation: If you use the brakes too much, they overheat and become less effective at stopping the vehicle.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a tire problem?

options.text: At least 2/32 inch of tread on rear tires

questions.correctAnswerText: At least 2/32 inch of tread on rear tires
questions.explanation: Check that air pressure is correct, front tires have at least 4/32 inch of tread, other tires have at least 2/32 inch of tread, and you do not mix radial and bias-ply tires together.

questions.question: For an offset back/left parking maneuver, what should you do?

options.text: Drive straight forward, then back to the right.
Drive straight forward, then back to the left.
Drive forward to the right, then back in a straight line.
Drive forward to the left, then back in a straight line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive straight forward, then back to the left.
questions.explanation: For an offset back/left parking maneuver, drive straight forward first, then back up to the left. Park your vehicle completely within the parking space boundaries.

questions.question: Before entering a curve, what should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to a lower gear.
questions.explanation: Shift to a lower gear before entering a curve. Slowing down before the curve helps you control your vehicle better while turning.

questions.question: When making a tight turn in a CMV, what should you do?

options.text: Drive as fast as a car driver would.
Ignore speed and focus only on the road.
Brake early and slow down gradually to warn drivers behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake early and slow down gradually to warn drivers behind you.
questions.explanation: Drivers behind you may not know how slowly your CMV needs to turn. Brake early and slow down gradually to give them warning in advance.

questions.question: What is the problem with eating while driving?

options.text: It is encouraged on long trips.
It takes your attention away from driving.
It is required to keep cargo supervised.

questions.correctAnswerText: It takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: Avoid eating, drinking, or smoking while driving. These activities distract you from focusing on the road.

questions.question: When should a driver use turn signals?

options.text: Always use turn signals when changing lanes.
Only use turn signals if another vehicle is next to you.
Do not use a turn signal if a lane change is obvious.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use turn signals when changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes. This tells other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.question: What affects how far your vehicle travels before stopping?
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on your vehicle's speed, its weight, and the grip the tires have on the road surface.

questions.question: What happens if an applicant does not get an air brakes endorsement?

options.text: They cannot operate a vehicle with air brakes.
They can only operate a vehicle with air brakes within the state.
They can only operate a vehicle with air brakes across state lines.

questions.correctAnswerText: They cannot operate a vehicle with air brakes.
questions.explanation: To drive a CMV with air brakes, you must pass the air brakes knowledge test and use a vehicle with air brakes for your skills test.

questions.question: How can you identify a distracted driver?

options.text: They are focused on using their cell phone.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are focused on using their cell phone.
questions.explanation: A distracted driver may drift between lanes, travel at uneven speeds, use a cell phone, look at maps, eat, or talk to passengers instead of watching the road.

questions.question: On a curve, is the posted speed limit always safe?

options.text: Yes, it is safe for any vehicle.
No, a vehicle can still tip over at the posted limit.
No, it is understood to be the minimum speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, a vehicle can still tip over at the posted limit.
questions.explanation: The posted speed limit may be safe for cars but too fast for larger vehicles like trucks. A truck driver traveling at the posted limit on a curve could cause their vehicle to tip over.

questions.question: How often must drivers check that cargo is secure?
questions.correctAnswerText: Every 150 miles.
questions.explanation: Check cargo security before starting, within the first 50 miles, and then every three hours or 150 miles after that.

questions.question: When traveling down a hill, what happens to your speed?

options.text: You will slow to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your speed will increase.
questions.explanation: Gravity pulls your vehicle faster as you go downhill. Your speed will naturally increase.

questions.question: You should always be able to stop within:

options.text: Your view of the road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your view of the road ahead.
questions.explanation: You must be able to stop within the distance you can see ahead. Slow down if you cannot see far enough to stop safely.

questions.question: When driving, keeping space between your vehicle and other vehicles is:
questions.correctAnswerText: Important.
questions.explanation: Keep space between your vehicle and others. This gives you room to stop safely without hitting someone else.

questions.question: ____ is a thin layer of ice that forms on road surfaces.
questions.correctAnswerText: Black ice
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin layer of clear ice on the road. It looks like wet pavement. Be careful when it is below freezing and the road looks wet.

questions.question: What kind of force must emergency brakes use?
questions.correctAnswerText: Mechanical
questions.explanation: Emergency brakes must use mechanical force because air pressure can leak away and fail.

questions.question: Which backing maneuver will NOT be in the basic control skills test?
questions.correctAnswerText: Blind offset
questions.explanation: The basic control skills test includes straight line backing, offset back/right, offset back/left, driver side parallel parking, conventional parallel parking, and alley docking. Blind offset is not included.

questions.question: Pressing and releasing the brake pedal unnecessarily can:

options.text: Release air faster than it can be replaced.
Add more air to a brake system.
Make the brake pedal harder to depress.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release air faster than it can be replaced.
questions.explanation: Pumping the brake pedal on an air brake system can let air out faster than the compressor can replace it. This can cause the system to lose pressure and the brakes to fail.

questions.question: The Individual Vehicle Distance Record (IVDR) must include all of the following, except:
questions.correctAnswerText: The number of stops.
questions.explanation: An IVDR must include trip dates, origin and destination, route, odometer readings, total distance, in-jurisdiction distance, and vehicle number. The number of stops is not required.

questions.question: To stop a vehicle with air brakes, the driver should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Push the brake pedal down.
questions.explanation: Push the brake pedal down to stop. The harder you push, the more air pressure is released to stop the vehicle.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver crashes on the road ahead of you, you should:

options.text: Block the driver in with your vehicle.
Stop after the crash scene and report the driver's aggressive behavior to the police.
Continue driving and mind your own business.
Pull over and yell at the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop after the crash scene and report the driver's aggressive behavior to the police.
questions.explanation: Stop a safe distance away from the crash. Wait for police to arrive and tell them about the aggressive driving you saw.

questions.question: When driving, your mirrors should:

options.text: Not be used because they distract you.
Not be used unless there is traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be checked regularly.
questions.explanation: You need to know what is around you at all times. Check your mirrors often while driving.

questions.question: When driving down a hill, when should you shift to a lower gear?

options.text: As you start to go downhill
As you go downhill and pick up speed

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start going downhill
questions.explanation: Slow down and shift to a lower gear before you start going downhill. If you don't, your brakes may get too hot and stop working properly.

questions.question: A Class 1 hazardous material is:
questions.correctAnswerText: An explosive.
questions.explanation: Explosives are in hazardous materials Class 1.

questions.question: After starting a trip while carrying cargo:

options.text: You do not need to inspect the cargo.
Check the cargo only if it is making noise.
Check the cargo only if something looks wrong.
Check the cargo after 50 miles to make sure it is still secure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the cargo after 50 miles to make sure it is still secure.
questions.explanation: Check your cargo before you start, within the first 50 miles, and then every three hours or every 150 miles to make sure it stays in place.

questions.question: When stopping a manual transmission vehicle, you should:

options.text: Push in the clutch when the engine is almost at idle.
Release the clutch when the engine is almost at idle.
Shift to neutral when the engine is almost at idle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push in the clutch when the engine is almost at idle.
questions.explanation: When stopping, press the brake pedal slowly and smoothly. For a manual transmission vehicle, push in the clutch when the engine is almost at idle.

questions.question: If you must write a vehicle inspection report, when must you sign it?

options.text: Only if problems were found and fixed.
Only if repairs cost more than $1,000.
Only if a police officer asks you to.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only if problems were found and fixed.
questions.explanation: Sign the previous vehicle inspection report only if problems were found and either fixed or did not need fixing.

questions.question: Always drive so your vehicle can stop:

options.text: Within the distance you can see ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Within the distance you can see ahead.
questions.explanation: Drive so you can stop your vehicle within the area of road you can see ahead if you need to.

questions.question: Front brake limiting valves were designed to:

options.text: Stop the front tires from skidding.
Stop the front tires from overheating.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the front tires from skidding.
questions.explanation: Some older air brake vehicles have front brake limiting valves. They were made to reduce front wheel skidding. However, research shows they are not needed, so they should stay in the "normal" position.

questions.question: When going down a steep hill:

options.text: Put the vehicle in a low gear and use engine braking.
Downshift instead of using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put the vehicle in a low gear and use engine braking.
questions.explanation: On long or steep hills, use engine braking to control your speed. Use your brakes only when you need extra stopping power.

questions.question: During an applied leakage test, what is the maximum leakage rate for a triple combination vehicle?
questions.correctAnswerText: 6 psi per minute.
questions.explanation: Know the safe maximum air loss rate for your vehicle. A triple combination vehicle should not leak more than 6 psi per minute during an applied leakage test.
